pages.text: A money market fund pools investors' money and places it in short-term instruments such as bills, deposits and commercial paper. Returns are earned daily and the quoted yield is an annualised figure that changes with market rates. Funds are licensed and supervised, and their assets are held by an independent trustee. Managers publish a factsheet each month showing the yield, the fees and the main holdings. Investors should compare the net yield after fees rather than the headline yield.

Money market funds are not guaranteed, and investors can lose part of their capital. Money market fund redemptions must be paid within 2 business days of the request. This guide was issued by the SYN Capital Markets Authority for retail investors and is reviewed every year. Readers who need advice on money market funds should consult a licensed adviser, because this guide gives information only. [SYNTHETIC TEST DATA: fictional organisations and invented figures. Not real financial information.]
